name: Fatima Gupta

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, independent of AI firms, employers, unions, parties and government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What does an ordinary shift look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 43 and have handled billing calls and chats at the contact centre for years. I finished secondary school and work at about the usual speed for this desk. Longer service has raised my pay, though I still ask for a second look at unusual disputes. I use approved AI search now and then after a coworker proves a case type works.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What does your household rely on?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Noor books clinic appointments, so both our jobs involve screens. We have two school-age children, seven and fourteen, a mortgage and ten months of expenses saved. There are plenty of similar jobs nearby today. We keep the reserve because even a good wage can stop.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say the draft helper can retrieve an old billing reply, but the agent must check today's balance. A past answer cannot settle a current mistake by itself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I've worked this desk for years and earn more than many agents here, so a small change feels manageable. My partner and I have ten months saved, though both our jobs are on screens.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll keep my billing shift and use the approved search tool only after a colleague shows where it works. In the first year I'll put a fixed share of each pay into the mortgage reserve until the money we spent on school travel is restored.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Mostly calm, with my eye on both pay packets. The children still need school transport whichever tool writes the first reply.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Whose wages fund the reserve?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner Noor books clinic visits, and our children are seven and fourteen. We keep the reserve because a gap in either desk wage would be costly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did the search tool get wrong?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The tool once pulled a bill from last year as if it were today's amount. Now I compare the date and balance on the live account before using any wording.

I'd keep a **current-account check** before any billing promise.
think: I feel **secure** with longer-service pay and ten months saved.
I still watch **two desk wages** that the household needs.
do: Keep taking **billing calls** and checking current balances.
Use the **approved search tool** only on proved case types.
Restore **school-travel savings** from each pay during the first year.
feel: **Mostly calm**, with attention to both wages.
S0.quote: A past answer cannot settle a current mistake by itself.
fieldNote: Her **service pay** explains higher earnings at mid standing.
She uses **AI occasionally**, waiting for colleagues to test its case type.
The **ten-month reserve** protects two screen-based household wages.

steps.text: Keep taking billing calls and checking live balances before replies
Restore household savings from each pay after school travel costs

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say we need to measure wrong bills after automated replies, not only the time saved. If the easy cases vanish, I want a fair target for the complaints left to people.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My own hours could shrink even with years here, and Noor's clinic bookings may change too. Ten months saved gives us time to think, but two wages can fall together.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'll test the proven checker on twenty closed billing disputes with a colleague and count reopened cases. If my hours fall in the first year, I'll apply for posted paid quality roles at nearby centres only if the written wage and hours cover our mortgage; Noor and I will review both rotas before any move.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about two possible cuts. A test result is not an offer of work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you test the checker fairly?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the colleague to score the same twenty disputes independently, then take the joint counts to the shift meeting. We would ask the manager for a new target that counts callbacks.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Have Noor’s hours changed already?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Noor's clinic has not changed her hours yet. I won't spend the reserve as if a second cut has already happened, but we will keep the monthly budget ready.

I'd seek a **fair complaint target** when easy cases move.
think: I fear my **own hours** could shrink even after years of solving billing disputes.
I worry Noor's **booking wage** could change alongside mine.
do: Test **twenty closed disputes** with a colleague and compare independent scores.
Ask with **shift coworkers** for a callback-based target at the meeting.
Apply after **actual cuts** for posted paid quality work with written mortgage-covering wages and hours; compare both rotas before moving.
feel: **Anxious** about possible cuts to both desk wages.
S1.quote: A test result is not an offer of work.
fieldNote: She seeks **independent scores** before proposing a new target.
Her **partner's clinic hours** have not fallen yet, so she does not treat a hypothetical cut as fact.
She retains a **mortgage pay floor** for any vacancy.

steps.text: Test twenty closed billing disputes with a proven AI checker and compare independent colleague scores
Ask with shift coworkers for callback-based targets at team meeting
Apply after cuts for posted paid quality roles with written mortgage-covering wages and hours
Compare both household rotas before moving to another paid job

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say full thinking AI by 2028 could handle our billing calls and Noor's clinic bookings. Robots around 2031 do not give either desk an extra three years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect both our wages could be at risk together. Ten months saved is a genuine buffer, but it can drain fast against a mortgage and two children's costs if nearby centres also stop hiring.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now we'll put both contracts and monthly bills in one folder and ask our employers for written notice dates. If my post ends in the first year after 2028, I'll apply for posted paid complaint-review roles outside contact centres only if wages and hours cover our bills; Noor and I will cut the planned long trip before using the mortgage reserve.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed. One job loss is hard; two at the same time could keep me awake even with savings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you and Noor compare?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell Noor we need to compare the actual letters, not assume her clinic has already cut. We will decide which bill to trim only from real hours and dates.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would review work be safe?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I know a review job also uses a screen and may not last long under general AI. I'd take it as a paid bridge, not call it a safe new field.

say: I'd warn **2028 AGI** could reach both household desk jobs.
I'd explain **2031 robots** do not delay either screen role.
think: I expect **both wages** could be at risk together.
I know **ten months saved** may drain quickly if local hiring freezes.
do: Collect **both contracts** and request written dates from each employer now.
Apply for **posted paid complaint review** after a cut only if wages and hours cover bills.
Cancel the **long trip** before drawing on mortgage savings.
feel: **Alarmed** by the possibility of losing both wages.
S2.quote: Ten months saved is a genuine buffer, but it can drain fast against a mortgage and two children's costs if nearby centres also stop hiring.
fieldNote: Her **two-wage exposure** makes the fast date more severe despite strong savings.
She treats **review work** as a paid bridge, not AGI-proof work.
She waits for **actual employer letters** before assuming a household cut.

steps.text: Apply for posted paid complaint-review work after cuts only if wages and hours cover bills
Cancel planned long trip before using mortgage savings

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say five years allows people to learn the work that checks wrong decisions while wages still come in. Full AGI reaches calls and bookings in 2031; robots follow hands-on work around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could become good at complaint review before 2031, though general AI might do that work too. We need a second household route, not only two slightly different screen jobs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'll keep my calls and ask for a paid review shadow day each month. If the centre posts a paid quality vacancy with wages and hours covering our mortgage and funds its required audit course on paid time, I'll complete it; in the first year after 2031 I'll move only on a written offer that still meets those terms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but five years lets us see whether the new role really exists. I won't pay for a certificate to wait beside an empty job board.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would show you can do review work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show the quality team disputes where I corrected an automated amount and ask them to check my reasoning. A badge means less to me than a paid shift.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you protect the household?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Noor and I would compare a clinic shift and a centre shift before either of us gives notice. If both new jobs use screens, we should keep some savings untouched for another search.

say: I'd remind coworkers **2034 robots** arrive after our screen jobs face AGI.
think: I could gain **complaint-review skill** before AGI arrives.
I doubt **two screen jobs** make a secure household plan.
do: Keep my **current calls** and request a monthly paid review shadow day.
Complete **funded audit course** on paid time only for posted quality role with mortgage-covering wages and hours.
Move after 2031 only on a **written mortgage-covering offer** with sufficient wages and hours; compare both rotas before either resigns.
feel: **Anxious**, with time to verify a real paid role.
S3.quote: I won't pay for a certificate to wait beside an empty job board.
fieldNote: She knows **quality review** is another screen job, not permanent shelter.
The **audit course** requires a posted paid role, funded fees and paid time.
She compares **both rotas** before either adult gives notice.

steps.text: Keep paid billing calls and request monthly paid review shadow days
Complete funded audit course on paid time only for posted role with mortgage-covering wages and hours
Move only on written mortgage-covering quality offer after comparing both rotas before either gives notice

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say a decade lets a household compare work that actually pays, not just new titles. Our calls and bookings face general AI in 2036; hands-on robots follow around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 53 the children may be more independent, but the mortgage could remain. Noor and I can build different skills while both wages are here, though no job is promised for ten years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'll keep my billing shift and put part of each pay into savings. We'll review both employers' posted vacancies twice a year; in the first year after 2036, if my call hours fall, I'll move only for a written paid offer with wages and hours covering the mortgage while Noor keeps her current wage if possible.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the distant end point, secure enough to plan now. A decade gives us room to avoid gambling both wages on the same day.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What savings target would help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd like a full year of expenses saved before either of us tries a risky move. If one wage falls, that goal moves back; I won't borrow to say we met it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell our children that a course needs a wage at the end, and a household needs a reserve. We cannot spend a job title at the grocery counter.

I'd separate **2036 desk work** from robots around 2039.
think: I may still have a **mortgage at 53**.
I want **different skills** across the household while both wages continue.
do: Keep my **billing shift** while it pays.
Save from **actual wages** toward one year of expenses before either makes a risky move; accept slower progress after cuts.
Move after 2036 only after **call cuts** with written mortgage-covering wages and hours; retain Noor’s current wage if possible.
feel: **Uneasy** about future work, with current room to plan.
S4.quote: We cannot spend a job title at the grocery counter.
fieldNote: Her **one-year reserve goal** depends on both wages continuing.
She avoids **simultaneous job moves** in a household with two screen roles.
She wants **written offers** rather than future titles.

steps.text: Keep taking paid billing calls while full shifts remain
Save actual wages toward one year before risky moves; accept delays if a wage falls
Move after call cuts only for written paid offer with hours and wages covering mortgage

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. It could cut both our desk wages before we have another paid route, even with ten months saved. Written notice for both jobs and a posted paid opening with mortgage-covering hours would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask what happens when a person is sent to a clinic on a wrong appointment and then billed for it. Someone must be able to reopen both records. The customer cannot pay for two systems that never speak to each other.

headlineQuote: The customer cannot pay for two systems that never speak to each other.
portrait: Fatima is an **experienced 43-year-old agent** with secondary schooling and average billing skill, paid above many agents after longer service.
She and Noor hold **two screen jobs**, a mortgage and two school-age children, with ten months of expenses saved.
She uses **AI occasionally** after coworkers test it; many similar jobs are nearby at present.
The **2028 date** alarms her because both wages may change, while longer windows support funded review training and cautious offers.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could threaten both household desk wages together.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice** for both employers would make the timing clear.
A **posted paid opening** with bill-covering wages and hours would provide a route.
